themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the system often changes itself while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization has no fixed baseline because models drift and personalize, incrementality testing is undermined by platforms that react to the holdout, identity resolution cannot be graded outside the logged-in minority, and lost B2B buying-group signal looks identical to a signal that was never real.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people who hold the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic all three models say agents have a commercial reason to look human and propose a faster, better agent-only lane instead of a protocol; journey orchestration stalls on channel owners paid for their own numbers; the semantic context layer is called a political settlement wearing a data modeling costume; and ad supply integrity stalls because the parties measuring the traffic profit from it.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: For safe agent execution every model proposes a proxy or gateway with hard spend, rate, and audience caps because sends and spend cannot be rolled back; consent enforcement answers route all data exits through a single checkpoint; and journey orchestration answers build one shared contact log that every channel must check before sending.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent and deletion answers agree that ad platforms and trained models are black boxes where removal cannot be proven, incrementality answers note platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and ad supply answers say fabricated impressions and engagement cannot be audited from outside.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers all build an approved-claims library and constrain what the model may say because implied meaning cannot be checked automatically, and the semantic context layer answers conclude that conflicting definitions of customer are legitimate and must be disclosed rather than merged.
